style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The most-quoted psalm in the New Testament, and only seven verses long. David overhears a conversation inside the Godhead -- the LORD's oracle to David's own Adon, his Lord: Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies the footstool of Your feet. Jesus put the psalm's riddle to the Pharisees and ended all questioning: if David calls Him Lord, how is He merely David's son? (Matthew 22:41-46). The psalm then unfolds the enthroned One's reign: the scepter of His strength sent out of Zion to rule in the very midst of His enemies; His people volunteering freely in the day of His power, arrayed in holy splendor, numerous and fresh as dew from the womb of the dawn. Verse 4 adds the second oracle, sealed with an oath God will never retract: You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek -- king and priest in one person, an office no son of Aaron could hold, which the letter to the Hebrews spends three chapters unfolding (Hebrews 5-7). The final movement is the day of wrath: kings shattered, nations judged, the head of the whole earth crushed -- and then the campaign's last quiet image, the Warrior stooping to drink from the brook beside the way, and lifting His head to finish the pursuit.

1.text: A psalm of David. The oracle of the LORD to my Lord: 'Sit at My right hand, until I set Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.'
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David. The LORD [YHWH] said [neum -- the solemn oracle of] unto my Lord [Adon -- my Sovereign], 'Sit [yashab] thou at My right hand [yamin], until I make [shith] thine enemies [oyeb] thy footstool [hadom] for thy feet [regel].'
1.notes: neum (H5002) is the prophet's oracle-word: David transcribes a conversation between YHWH (H3068) and his own Adon (H113) -- the king's King. Session at the yamin (H3225) is co-regency, and the footstool the ancient victory-rite of the foot on the conquered neck. The New Testament quotes or echoes this verse over twenty times (cf. Matthew 22:44; Acts 2:34-35; Hebrews 1:13).

2.text: The LORD will stretch out the scepter of Your strength from Zion: rule in the very midst of Your enemies.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall send [shalach] the rod [matteh -- the scepter, the staff] of thy strength [oz] out of Zion [Tsiyyon]: rule [radah -- have dominion] thou in the midst [qereb] of thine enemies [oyeb].
2.notes: The matteh oz (H4294, H5797), the scepter of strength, extends from Tsiyyon while the King sits enthroned above: His reign advances by His word going out (cf. the gospel from Jerusalem, Acts 1:8). radah (H7287) in the qereb (H7130) of enemies -- dominion exercised not after opposition ends but in the thick of it.

3.text: Your people will offer themselves as freewill offerings in the day of Your power, arrayed in the splendors of holiness; from the womb of the dawn, the dew of Your youth is Yours.
3.amp: Thy people [am] shall be willing [nedabah -- freewill offerings] in the day [yom] of thy power [chayil], in the beauties [hadar -- the splendors] of holiness [qodesh] from the womb [rechem] of the morning [mishchar -- the dawn]: thou hast the dew [tal] of thy youth [yalduth].
3.notes: nedabah (H5071) is the freewill offering itself: the King's army enlists as living sacrifices, no conscription (cf. Romans 12:1). They muster in hadar qodesh (H1926, H6944), priestly splendor rather than armor -- and the picture closes with numbers: like tal (H2919) from the dawn's own womb, countless, sudden, and glistening young.

4.text: The LORD has sworn and will not relent: 'You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.'
4.amp: The LORD [YHWH] has sworn [shaba], and will not repent [nacham -- relent, change His mind], 'Thou art a priest [kohen] for ever [olam] after the order [dibrah -- the manner] of Melchizedek [Malki-Tsedeq -- King of Righteousness].'
4.notes: The second oracle carries an oath: shaba (H7650) with nacham (H5162) forsworn -- immutable by God's own word (cf. Hebrews 7:20-21). Malki-Tsedeq (H4442), the king-priest of Salem who blessed Abraham (cf. Genesis 14:18), holds crown and priesthood in one person: an order older than Aaron, without genealogy or term -- kohen le-olam, the priesthood Hebrews builds its whole argument on (cf. Hebrews 7).

5.text: The Lord is at Your right hand; He shatters kings in the day of His wrath.
5.amp: The Lord [Adonai] at thy right hand [yamin] shall strike through [machats -- shatter, smite through] kings [melek] in the day [yom] of his wrath [aph].
5.notes: The camera reverses: the One seated AT the right hand now stands as champion at His people's right hand -- yamin (H3225) working both directions. machats (H4272) is the skull-crushing verb of Numbers 24:17; the yom aph, the day of wrath, is the fixed appointment the slow mercy of history precedes (cf. Revelation 6:16-17).

6.text: He will execute judgment among the nations, heaping up the dead; He will crush the head that rules the wide earth.
6.amp: He shall judge [din] among the heathen [goy -- the nations], he shall fill [male] the places with the dead bodies [geviyyah]; he shall wound [machats -- crush] the heads [rosh] over many ['great', rav, the KJV margin] countries [eretz].
6.notes: din (H1777), formal judgment executed at battlefield scale. The singular reading of the last clause -- the rosh (H7218) over the wide eretz crushed -- reaches back to Eden's sentence on the serpent's head (cf. Genesis 3:15) and forward to the final overthrow (cf. Revelation 19:11-21): the King's last enemy is the usurping head himself.

7.text: He will drink from the brook beside the way; therefore He will lift up His head.
7.amp: He shall drink [shatah] of the brook [nachal] in the way [derek]: therefore shall he lift up [rum] the head [rosh].
7.notes: The campaign's closing image, startlingly humble: the Warrior-King pausing at the nachal (H5158) like Gideon's men (cf. Judges 7:5-6), refreshed mid-pursuit and pressing on. The lifted rosh answers the crushed rosh of verse 6 -- and echoes the humiliation-then-exaltation arc the whole psalm sings: He stooped to the brook of our nature, therefore God highly exalted Him (cf. Philippians 2:8-9).
